skill.name: anatomy
skill.description: Create detailed interactive isometric SVG figures that explain technical concepts through physical mechanisms, with optional WebGL effects and React components.
skill.summary: Build technical explainers with shaded geometry, model-driven motion, and browser verification.
skill.author: wheresryan22

security_audit.summary: Most presented matches are benign geometry, documentation, local screenshots, and loopback browser control; no evidence found of prompt injection or intentional exfiltration. CLI-selected imports execute host code, and browser checks relax local-file isolation. Three oversized files and 2,518 omitted matches remain review gaps; this audit does not establish complete repository safety. Static review was capped at 400/2918 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 2518 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.
Remove cross-file access by default. Serve assets from a restricted local directory, or require explicit consent and filesystem isolation for file-mode checks.

remediation.issue: Verification imports execute user-selected modules with host privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted build targets and explicit execution consent. Run unknown modules in a sandbox without credentials, unrestricted filesystem access, or network access.

remediation.issue: Oversized files and capped static results leave incomplete security coverage.
remediation.suggestion: Review all three skipped HTML files and the 2,518 omitted matches. Provide reproducible builds and smaller reviewable artifacts before automatic publication.

content.value_statement: Technical concepts can be difficult to explain with static diagrams. Anatomy guides assistants to build detailed physical mechanisms with interactive motion and consistent numeric readouts.
actual_capabilities: Build shaded isometric solids, round parts, pipes, and cables with the included drawing kit.
Generate standalone HTML pages, styled SVG files, and React or Next.js figure components.
Drive pointer interactions, keyboard controls, motion, and numeric readouts from a shared model.
Combine SVG geometry with registered WebGL effects for water, light, exhaust, and steam.
Check geometry clearance, support, depth ordering, and line endpoints with included verification tools.
Capture browser screenshots, close-ups, and motion contact sheets in light and dark themes.
limitations: Node.js is required for builds; Chrome or Chromium is required for browser checks.
Shader effects require WebGL; fallback views retain SVG geometry without those effects.
The optional 3D mode is beta, and dense scenes can perform poorly on mobile devices.
Verification can be slow, and executable build modules and local pages require trust.

use_cases.title: Explain Software Mechanisms
use_cases.description: Create interactive figures for caching, rate limiting, or connection pooling, using supplied counts and thresholds.

use_cases.title: Integrate Documentation Figures
use_cases.description: Add reusable React or Next.js figures with static geometry, client-side motion, and model-driven readouts.

use_cases.title: Demonstrate Physical Processes
use_cases.description: Build instrument or machine explainers with moving parts and optional WebGL water, lighting, or exhaust effects.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Anatomy to explain a token bucket with 20 tokens and a refill rate of five tokens per second. Produce light standalone HTML.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one concept and one deliverable.

prompt_templates.title: Add Model-Driven Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an interactive connection-pooling figure with ten connections and a waiting queue. Include keyboard controls, accurate readouts, both themes, and mobile screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a React Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React figure explaining cache hits, misses, and a 60-second TTL. Separate static geometry from client motion and provide an HTML preview.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Verify a Shader Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ripple-tank explainer with SVG apparatus and registered WebGL water effects. Verify geometry, reduced motion, shader transitions, and fallback rendering on trusted local pages.

output_examples.input: Explain token-bucket rate limiting with 20 tokens and five new tokens per second.
output: A standalone light HTML figure represents token storage and request consumption as a working mechanism.
Controls trigger requests, and a readout shows available tokens and rejected requests.
The deliverables include the build source and browser previews.

output_examples.input: Create a React explainer for a pool of ten database connections.
output: A static geometry component displays ten connection slots and a request queue.
A client component animates borrowing and returning connections from one shared model.
A standalone preview supports review before application integration.

output_examples.input: Show water ripples with SVG apparatus and WebGL effects.
output: An interactive tank figure aligns water reflections and projected caustics with the SVG camera.
Frequency controls update the wave model and readout.
Fallback and reduced-motion views preserve a readable apparatus.

best_practices: Provide the concept, real numeric parameters, output format, and theme before requesting geometry.
Keep motion and readouts connected to one model, then review both themes and mobile dimensions.
Inspect build modules and pages before verification; isolate unknown content and review screenshots before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not replace the mechanism with decorative boxes or unrelated animation.
Do not hide geometry failures with depth biases or inaccurate recorded shapes.
Do not run unknown build modules or local pages with unrestricted verification privileges.

faq.question: Which assistants can use Anatomy?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility. The upstream workflow is written primarily for Claude Code.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The kit supports standalone HTML, styled SVG files, and React or Next.js components.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: Builds require Node.js 20.10 or later. Browser checks need Chrome or Chromium; React output requires React 18 or later.

faq.question: Does every figure need WebGL?
faq.answer: No. SVG is the core format. WebGL adds effects such as water, fire, lighting, and steam.

faq.question: Is the 3D mode production-ready?
faq.answer: The upstream documentation labels it beta. Dense moving scenes can be slow, and verification can take substantial time.

faq.question: What security precautions are needed?
faq.answer: Use trusted build modules and pages. Imports run host code, browser checks enable cross-file access, and capped analysis leaves unresolved review gaps.
